subject: Re: Urgent — production 504s and retry amplification impacting Northbridge Health
messages:
From: Elaine Harris <elaine.harris@northbridgehealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Northbridge Health EngOps <engops@northbridgehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 18:04:00 -0700
Subject: Production 504s — page sent us a major alert

Hi Irene,

We're seeing a sharp increase in 504s and 429s from the Redwood endpoint behind our triage API starting ~17:40 PDT. Latency has climbed from 120ms p50 to 3–8s p95 and many requests are returning 504. Our retries are amplifying the issue and it's cascading into timeouts on our side.

Attached is a short metrics snapshot and a small trace snippet. We rely on this inference flow for patient triage in our mobile app — this is blocking a portion of traffic. Can you confirm receipt and provide immediate mitigation steps? We need ETA on a fix and whether you can temporarily route us to a lower-capacity fallback model or a different region.

Thanks,
Elaine Harris
Director, Platform Engineering
Northbridge Health

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Harris <elaine.harris@northbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 18:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production 504s — page sent us a major alert

Elaine — thanks for the quick heads up and the artifacts. We see the same signal in our platform telemetry. I'm escalating to infra and routing to exec ops. Immediate next steps:

- I have put your traffic on debug sampling to collect full traces.
- Monica, Karthik, Markus — can you triage the batching/KV-cache layers? Attachments show rapid prefix misses and a dropped batch queue.
- Elaine: can you confirm whether you are using sticky routing to a dedicated pool or the shared hosted endpoint? If you can switch to the alternate region temporarily we can route you there while we investigate.

We will follow up in 30 minutes with an action plan. Apologies for the outage impact — we're treating this as Sev1.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elaine Harris <elaine.harris@northbridgehealth.com>, Northbridge Health EngOps <engops@northbridgehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production 504s — initial findings and mitigations

Team, Elaine — quick update from infra investigation:

Observations:
- Between 17:35–18:00 PDT we see a sudden rise in queue depth for the VCPU-to-GPU dispatch queues servicing NBH jobs.
- KV-cache miss rate jumped ~12x for short prefixes; that aligns with the customer's trace where the client TTL for conversation context was slightly reduced yesterday.
- Batching layer reacted by trying to maintain throughput, but due to cache miss storms we observed multiple large batches being dropped at the forwarder when latency exceeded our per-batch SLO -> resulting in 504s and retry waves.
- Retries from the client side (backoff 0.5–2s) amplified queueing and caused a retry storm.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:00 PDT):
1) Temporarily reduced batch size ceiling for NBH routing key to 1. This sacrifices throughput but prevents large batch eviction and reduces p95 latency.
2) Enabled per-customer prefix caching hold (sticky KV) to reduce misses for short context windows.
3) Applied aggressive retry-throttling at the gateway for the NBH route (100qps cap) and returned a Retry-After header for excess requests.

Next steps:
- We're rolling a patch to the KV eviction policy to prevent synchronized TTL expirations (predictable rollout over next 2–3 hours).
- Markus to produce a short runbook for customers on how to avoid client-side retry amplification.

Elaine: would you like us to fail over your route to eu-west-1 while the patch lands? That would give immediate relief if your clients can tolerate the region change.

-Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
[inline trace id: rwd-20270309-ny1-774]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Harris <elaine.harris@northbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 11:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production 504s — status, timeline, and executive summary

Elaine — summary and next steps following today's mitigation work:

What happened (short):
- A synchronized spike in KV-cache misses combined with client-side aggressive retries caused large batch evictions and queue saturation. Those evictions increased tail latency and produced 504s; retries amplified the spike into a retry storm.

What we did:
- Applied per-customer batching cap and enabled sticky-prefix caching to stabilize miss-rate.
- Throttled retries at the gateway and surfaced Retry-After so your clients back off cleanly.
- Deployed a targeted KV-eviction policy patch (rolled to 30% of hosts at 10:45 PDT) to desynchronize TTL expirations.

Current status:
- Error rate has returned to baseline (~0.6% 5xx) and p95 latency is down to ~420ms for NBH traffic.
- We kept your traffic on the hosted pool but with reduced batch ceiling. Throughput is ~70% of normal for the affected route.

Timeline & next steps:
- 12:30 PDT: complete rollout of eviction patch (estimate).
- 13:00 PDT: rollback batching cap and run controlled load to validate.
- Within 48 hours: follow-up postmortem with root cause, mitigations, and recommended client-side retry/backoff settings.

In parallel we will:
- Add a per-route retry amplification detector to alert before queue saturation.
- Publish a KB for customers with recommended sticky-routing and retry backoff guidance.

If you'd prefer an immediate region failover while we finish the patch, we can do that now — please confirm. Otherwise we'll proceed with the plan above.

Apologies again for the disruption; we understand the impact on Northbridge. Monica and I are available for a call with your ops/exec team to walk through details.

Best regards,
Irene Choi
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference
